subject: Hosted API commit pathway — renewal + upsell workplan
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Molly Chen <molly@olivetech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API commit pathway — renewal + upsell workplan

Hi Molly —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Per our call, I wanted to capture a compact workplan so we can align timelines for OliveTech’s renewal and the proposed hosted commit increase. TL;DR: OliveTech would move from the current 2.5M token/month commit to a phased 5M token/month commit with a 12-month term; we recommend a 3-month canary (soft throttle/burst guardrail) and a 10% volume discount on the extra commit band.

Key items for next week:
- Finalize committed volume and billing cadence (you mentioned finance prefers monthly invoices).
- Procurement to confirm acceptable contract language for data retention and audit logs.
- Ops: schedule a brief runbook review for rate limit windows and burst cushions.
- Legal: review amendment that preserves existing SLA but adds a higher-rateband for the additional commit.

I attached a draft playbook and a first pass addendum (Hosted_Commit_Addendum_v3.pdf). Ben is on copy for pricing confirmation and to coordinate the DocuSign flow. If procurement needs specific KMS/HSM language or SOC-2 references, loop them in and we’ll pull our security pack.

Proposed timeline:
- 2027-04-21: Procurement questions due
- 2027-04-23: Redwood provides redline-ready addendum
- 2027-04-26: Target sign (DocuSign) and go-live window scheduling

Are you good with that cadence? If OliveTech prefers quarterly invoicing instead of monthly, we can accommodate (pricing will adjust).

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0189

Attachments referenced: Hosted_Commit_Addendum_v3.pdf, OliveTech_Renewal_Playbook_v1.xlsx
From: Molly Chen <molly@olivetech.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit pathway — renewal + upsell workplan

Thanks Hannah — this looks good as an outline. A few follow-ups from finance/procurement: 1) can you confirm the effective rate for the incremental tokens (the 10% discount you mentioned) in $/1k tokens so my finance team can model costs; 2) our procurement lead asked for language around data deletion timeline (we need a 90-day requirement after contract end); 3) what happens to soft throttle behavior if we hit sudden seasonal spikes — will OliveTech get temporary burst credits or will requests be rejected?

Also: we prefer quarterly invoicing for cashflow planning, but if monthly makes the pricing materially better we may consider switching. Will let procurement follow up directly on the addendum redlines.

Molly
Molly Chen | Head of ML Platforms, OliveTech
molly@olivetech.com | +1 323-555-0193
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Molly Chen <molly@olivetech.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit pathway — renewal + upsell workplan

Hannah — copied for awareness and to answer Molly’s questions. Quick notes: 

1) Incremental rate: base-band rate remains as currently contracted. For the extra 2.5M tokens/month we propose $0.65 per 1k tokens (effective 10% off the published extra-band rate). I’ll call this out in the addendum.

2) Data deletion: we can include a 90-day data deletion obligation post-term for inference logs and prompt storage; full audit trail metadata for 365 days can be retained if needed. We should flag this to security for a final sign-off.

3) Soft throttle / bursts: proposed behavior: 
   - Canary (first 90 days): autoscale burst pool up to 1.5x commit for short spikes, with notification and manual ops review if sustained beyond 10 minutes.
   - Post-canary: soft throttle thresholds applied at 1.25x sustained for >5 minutes; temporary burst credits can be applied (one-time per quarter) subject to approval.

If procurement wants the 90-day deletion clause in the addendum language, I’ll update v3 to v4 and resend. Also note: switching from monthly to quarterly invoicing increases billing cycle risk and we’d recommend a small uplift (1.5%) to the effective rate to offset cashflow.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Renewals & Expansion, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Molly Chen <molly@olivetech.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit pathway — renewal + upsell workplan

Thanks Molly — appreciate the questions. Quick replies inline and next steps below.

> can you confirm the effective rate for the incremental tokens (the 10% discount you mentioned) in $/1k tokens

Ben has confirmed: $0.65 / 1k tokens for the incremental band (we’ll put this in the pricing table of the addendum).

> our procurement lead asked for language around data deletion timeline (we need a 90-day requirement after contract end)

Agreed — Ben will push Hosted_Commit_Addendum_v4 that includes a 90-day deletion clause for prompt/inference payloads and 365-day audit metadata retention.

> what happens to soft throttle behavior if we hit sudden seasonal spikes

Operational behavior: during the first 90-day canary we allow 1.5x burst auto-scaling for brief spikes with automated notification to OliveTech’s SREs; sustained spikes (beyond 10 minutes) trigger ops review and manual approval for sustained burst credits. Post-canary we have the soft throttle thresholds and one-time quarterly burst credit policy as Ben called out.

Next steps / asks:
- Ben: please produce addendum v4 with pricing table, 90-day deletion clause, and the burst-credit language by EOD 2027-04-25.
- Molly / Procurement: confirm whether quarterly invoicing is preferred (we can accept with a 1.5% uplift) or if you’ll keep monthly to retain the posted pricing.
- Karthik / Ops: if you can block a 30-minute runbook sync with OliveTech SREs the week of 2027-04-28, that should get the go-live prep done.

I’ve attached the playbook (OliveTech_Renewal_Playbook_v1.xlsx) and I’ll route v4 once Ben updates it. If procurement wants to route redlines, we’ll accept them via HubSpot or DocuSign markup — whichever is easiest for you.

Cheers —
Hannah
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
